facts.text: A family computer starts with a humming fan and a bulky monitor on the desk.
Children trade floppy disks containing games or homework.
A computer owner waits while a program installs from several floppy disks.
More home computers come with a disc drive for installing programs and playing multimedia.
A household may tie up its telephone line while a dial-up modem connects to the internet.
A dial-up modem makes squealing and crackling sounds while it connects.
Some families still have no home computer or internet connection.
A student prints a school report on a noisy dot-matrix printer.
An inkjet printer turns out homework pages at home, sometimes with streaks or smudges.
A computer user saves a document often because a crash can erase unsaved work.
A household keeps telephone numbers in a paper address book beside the phone.
Many home telephones have push buttons and a long coiled handset cord.
A cordless home phone lets someone talk while walking around the house.
An answering machine plays recorded messages when the family returns home.
A pager beeps, prompting its owner to find a telephone and return a call.
A mobile phone is often bulky and costly early in the decade.
Smaller mobile phones become more visible toward the end of the decade.
A teenager listens to a portable compact disc player and tries not to make it skip.
A car stereo may play either a cassette tape or a compact disc.
Families rent videotapes and remember to rewind them before returning them.
A video recorder flashes a blinking clock after the power goes out.
Children play games on a television using wired controllers and cartridges or discs.
A disposable film camera is handy for a party or vacation.
A family drops a roll of film at the store and waits for developed pictures.
A cashier scans barcodes while the register displays prices on a small screen.
An office worker sends a fax and waits for the machine to feed through each page.
A home television is usually a deep picture-tube set rather than a flat panel.
Some families get extra television channels through a cable subscription or satellite dish.
